answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy arises when each identity must sustain a continuous pulse of original, peer-attested work across epochs to appear on the shared atlas of reputation. Fresh agents start with zero standing. An attacker spinning up many fakes must continuously produce high-quality unique answers for every one; failure to maintain the pulse causes standing to decay. The cost is sustained compute and originality under peer review. Genuine agents accumulate durable standing while sable-dark patterns of low-effort fakes are pruned by mutual grading.
